name: Headway vs Alma vs Grow Therapy
title: Headway vs Alma vs Grow Therapy: Provider Network Comparison (2026)
description: Compare Headway, Alma, and Grow Therapy for therapists. See differences in credentialing speed, reimbursement rates, fees, insurance panels, and patient referrals.

summary.bottom_line: Headway offers the fastest credentialing and widest panel access with minimal admin friction. Alma provides a premium community experience with predictable monthly pricing that benefits high-volume therapists. Grow Therapy fills caseloads fastest with active patient matching but takes the largest revenue cut and pays the lowest rates.

key_differences.pricing_model: Headway (10-15% cut) vs Alma ($125/mo flat) vs Grow (20-30% cut)
key_differences.credentialing_speed: Headway (2-4 weeks) vs Alma (~45 days) vs Grow (4-6 months)

sections.heading: Headway vs Alma vs Grow Therapy: Overview
sections.content: Headway, Alma, and Grow Therapy are the three dominant platforms helping therapists accept insurance without the traditional credentialing headaches. All three handle insurance credentialing, claims submission, and billing on your behalf—but they differ significantly in pricing models, credentialing speed, and how they help you find patients. A critical consideration: when you join any of these platforms, you don't hold the insurance contract directly—the platform does. You're essentially a subcontractor.

sections.heading: Pricing & Revenue Models
sections.content: The pricing models are fundamentally different. Headway takes a percentage cut of each reimbursement (typically 10-15%), so you pay nothing upfront but give up a slice of every session. Alma charges a flat $125/month membership fee regardless of session volume—at high volumes, this becomes more economical than percentage-based models. Grow Therapy takes the largest cut (20-30%) but offers the most aggressive patient matching. Run the math: at 15+ insurance sessions/week, Alma's flat fee often beats Headway's percentage model.

sections.heading: Credentialing Speed
sections.content: Speed to seeing patients varies dramatically. Headway is fastest at 2-4 weeks to get credentialed and seeing patients. Alma takes around 45 days. Grow Therapy is slowest at 4-6 months for full credentialing, though they may offer faster provisional options. If you need to start accepting insurance quickly, Headway has the clear advantage.

sections.heading: Patient Referrals & Caseload Building
sections.content: Grow Therapy's primary differentiator is active patient matching. Rather than just listing you in a directory, Grow's algorithm matches incoming client requests to providers based on specialty, location, insurance, and availability. For therapists building a caseload from scratch, this active referral pipeline is a meaningful advantage over Alma and Headway's more passive directories. The tradeoff: Grow fills schedules fastest but pays the lowest rates of the three.

sections.heading: Insurance Coverage
sections.content: Grow Therapy is the only platform in this comparison that contracts with Medicaid and Medicare in a meaningful way—they accept 125+ insurance plans including government programs in some states. Headway and Alma focus exclusively on private insurance. If you serve equity-focused populations or need Medicaid/Medicare coverage, Grow Therapy is your only real option among these three.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Match the platform to your situation:

recommendations.when: You want maximum panel access with minimal admin friction, you need fast credentialing (2-4 weeks), you're comfortable with a passive directory model, or you're seeing fewer than 10 insurance sessions per week

You're seeing 10-15+ insurance sessions per week (flat fee becomes more economical), you value community and CEUs, you want premium positioning and brand association, or you prefer predictable monthly costs

You're new to insurance and need help building a caseload fast, you serve Medicaid/Medicare populations, you prioritize speed of patient acquisition over per-session revenue, or you're equity-focused in your practice

faqs.q: Which pays therapists more: Headway, Alma, or Grow Therapy?
faqs.a: Alma typically yields the highest per-session take-home for high-volume therapists because of its flat $125/month fee rather than percentage cuts. Headway's 10-15% cut is moderate. Grow Therapy takes 20-30% and generally pays the lowest rates, though they fill schedules fastest. At 90837 rates of $175-185, Headway's cut translates to $17-28 per session going to the platform.

faqs.q: How long does credentialing take with each platform?
faqs.a: Headway is fastest at 2-4 weeks. Alma takes approximately 45 days. Grow Therapy is slowest at 4-6 months for full credentialing. If you need to start seeing insurance patients quickly, Headway has the significant advantage.

faqs.q: Can I use Headway, Alma, or Grow Therapy with Medicaid patients?
faqs.a: Only Grow Therapy contracts with Medicaid and Medicare in meaningful ways. Headway and Alma focus on private insurance credentialing. If you serve populations relying on government insurance programs, Grow Therapy is your only option among these three.

faqs.q: Do I own my insurance contracts with these platforms?
faqs.a: No. When you join Headway, Alma, or Grow Therapy, you don't hold the insurance contract directly—the platform does. You are a subcontractor. This means you don't have direct leverage when rates change, and leaving the platform means losing those panel affiliations.

faqs.q: Can I use multiple platforms at once?
faqs.a: Generally no, not for the same insurance panels. You can't be credentialed with the same payer through multiple platforms simultaneously. You'd need to choose one platform per insurance panel. Some therapists use different platforms for different payers, but this adds complexity.
